{
  "abstract_verbatim": "Equality in the spacetime Penrose inequality identifies the original initial data as a spacelike slice of a Schwarzschild–Tangherlini exterior, smoothly attached to its horizon, under the stated outermostness and decay hypotheses. We prove this in every spatial dimension <i>n</i> ≥ 3 for a strong-decay exterior class and for weaker decay in dimensions three and four. In dimension three the finite-component theorem forces a single spherical horizon and gives qualitative strictness for disconnected boundaries.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> Equality in the spacetime Penrose inequality identifies the original initial data as a spacelike slice of a Schwarzschild–Tangherlini exterior, smoothly attached to its horizon, under the stated outermostness and decay hypotheses. We prove this in every spatial dimension <i>n</i> ≥ 3 for a strong-decay exterior class and for weaker decay in dimensions three and four. In dimension three the finite-component theorem forces a single spherical horizon and gives qualitative strictness for disconnected boundaries.

- **C1** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-numerical-input)): The numerical spacetime Penrose theorem (OpenAI 2026b, Theorem 1.3) [[CompanionNumerical](#ref-CompanionNumerical)] states that every initial-data exterior in Definition <a href="#def:data" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:data">1</a>, with the positive full-cut infimum in Definition <a href="#def:fullcuts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:fullcuts">2</a>, satisfies $$\boxed{\quad m\ge\frac12 \left(\frac{A_{\min}(S)}{\omega}\right)^{\frac{n-2}{n-1}} . \quad} \label{eq:setting:main}$$ This input is used for nearby weakly trapped data as well as for the original pair. It imposes none of the additional equality hypotheses introduced below.
  - Explanation: The enclosing-area comparison applies to weakly trapped variations without the additional rigidity assumptions.
- **C2** (classification, [source](#stmt-thm-rigidity)): Suppose an exterior in Definition <a href="#def:setting:rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:setting:rigidity">4</a> attains equality in <a href="#eq:setting:main" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:setting:main">[eq:setting:main]</a>. There is a global smooth spacelike embedding of the entire $\Omega$, including $S$, into the regular extension of one exterior of $\mathbf G_m$, inducing exactly the original $g$ and $K$ with convention <a href="#eq:setting:Ksign" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:setting:Ksign">[eq:setting:Ksign]</a>.* *The image lies in the domain $r>r_m$ together with its corresponding future horizon and bifurcation sphere. The boundary maps to a full smooth section of that future horizon or to its bifurcation sphere. The embedding and future unit normal extend smoothly to $S$ in horizon-regular coordinates, and the chosen end approaches spatial infinity. There is no conclusion about a region behind $S$.
  - Explanation: Equality identifies the original metric and second fundamental form with a smooth spacelike Schwarzschild–Tangherlini slice, including its horizon attachment. The conclusion concerns the exterior.
- **C3** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-converse)): Let $M>0$. Every smooth spacelike exterior hypersurface in the regular extension of $\mathbf G_M$, with its interior in $r>r_M$, whose induced data satisfy Definitions <a href="#def:data" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:data">1</a>, <a href="#def:fullcuts" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:fullcuts">2</a>, and <a href="#def:setting:rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:setting:rigidity">4</a>, whose boundary is a full smooth section of the corresponding future horizon or its bifurcation sphere, and whose end approaches spatial infinity, has $$(E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2)^{1/2}=M,\qquad A=\omega(2M)^{\frac{n-1}{n-2}}. \label{eq:setting:converse}$$ It therefore attains equality in <a href="#eq:setting:main" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:setting:main">[eq:setting:main]</a>. In every dimension there are admissible static examples and admissible examples with $K\not\equiv0$.
  - Explanation: Admissible Schwarzschild–Tangherlini slices attain equality, including non-time-symmetric slices and slices with asymptotic boosts.
- **C4** (construction, [source](#stmt-q-geometry-enclosure)): The minimum in Equation <a href="#q:geometry:full-perimeter" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q:geometry:full-perimeter">[q:geometry:full-perimeter]</a> exists, equals $a(g)>0$, and is independent of the filling. All its minimizing sets are contained in one compact region. Their multiplicity-one frontiers are smooth minimal hypersurfaces away from $B$ and a singular set of Hausdorff dimension at most $n-8$; the singular set is empty when $n\le7$. Every contact point with $B$ is regular, with a $C^{1,\alpha}\cap W^{2,p}$ graph for every finite $p$ and $0<\alpha<1$. For $n=3,4$ the whole frontier is $C^{1,1}$, including contact, and its graph functions are $W^{2,\infty}$.* *In dimensions $3$ and $4$, each frontier bounds a connected exterior and is the $C^1$ and area limit of smooth full cuts contained in $\operatorname{int}X$. If $H_B<0$ for the normal into $X$, every minimizer contains one fixed exterior collar of $B$. In dimensions $3$ and $4$ its frontier is then a smooth minimal full cut; its closed exterior is connected, one-ended, complete with its boundary included, and outer area-minimizing with all boundary components counted. In every dimension, whenever a minimizing frontier is smooth, its closed exterior has these same connectedness, completeness, one-end and outer area-minimization properties.
  - Explanation: The full-perimeter infimum has compact minimizing frontiers, with dimension-dependent regularity and strict-barrier detachment.
- **C5** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q-geometry-envelope)): The space $\mathcal T(g)$ is compact and metrizable. For every smooth symmetric two-tensor $h$ the function $$E\longmapsto a'_E(h):= \frac12\int_{\partial^*E}\operatorname{tr}_{T\partial^*E}h\,dA_g$$ is continuous on it. Let $g_t$, $\|t\|<t_0$, be a smooth path of smooth metrics with $g_0=g$, extended smoothly through the fixed boundary. Assume uniform comparison with $g$, and bounded first and second parameter derivatives relative to $g$. One sufficient end hypothesis is $$\label{q:geometry:uniform-AF} g_t-\delta=O_2(r^{-q_*})\quad\hbox{uniformly for }\|t\|<t_0, \qquad q_*>0.$$ More generally, it suffices that the coordinate spheres have positive outward mean curvature beyond one common radius. The result also holds if the end metrics are uniformly comparable to the Euclidean metric with uniform scaled $C^1$ bounds; they need not have a common mean-convex tail in this last alternative. Put $h=\partial_tg_t\|_0$. Then $$\label{q:geometry:envelope-derivative} \left.\frac{d}{dt}\right\|_{0+}a(g_t) =\min_{E\in\mathcal T(g)}a'_E(h).$$ For any $t_j\to0$ and any $E_j\in\mathcal T(g_{t_j})$, a subsequence converges in $L^1$ to $E\in\mathcal T(g)$, with convergence of perimeters and of the plane measures computed in the fixed metric $g$.
  - Explanation: The least-area envelope has a right derivative given by the smallest first area variation over its compact minimizing family.
- **C6** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-variation-multiplier)): There are a probability measure $\pi$ on $\mathfrak T$, a locally finite nonnegative measure $\Lambda$ on $\mathfrak A$, and a finite nonnegative measure $\zeta$ on $S$, such that $$\label{eq:variation:multiplier} 2k\omega\mathcal E'(h,p)-c\int_{\mathfrak T}a'_C(h)\,d\pi(C) =\int_{\mathfrak A}\mathfrak C'(h,p;v)\,d\Lambda(x,v) -\int_S\theta'_+(h,p)\,d\zeta.$$ This identity holds for all smooth compactly supported variations, including arbitrary jets at $S$, and for the energy and momentum prototypes specified below. The scalar and vector moments of $\Lambda$ obey, initially as measures, $$\label{eq:variation:causality} u\ge \|X\|_g,\qquad u\mu+J(X)=0.$$ Here a field and its density relative to the fixed original volume form are identified when that density exists.
  - Explanation: A positive measure separator represents the active constraints and all minimizing enclosures; its moments satisfy causality and complementarity.
- **C7** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-variation-common-jacobi)): Let $C\in\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\pi$ belong to the full-measure family in Lemma <a href="#lem:variation:contact-dichotomy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:variation:contact-dichotomy">16</a>, with wholly interior frontier, and let $\Sigma$ be a connected component of its regular part. If its local graph parameter at some patch is not an atom, there is a smooth positive function $\varphi$ on all of $\Sigma$ with $$\label{eq:variation:common-jacobi} L_0\varphi=L_+\varphi=L_-\varphi=0.$$
  - Explanation: Neighboring non-atomic minimizing sheets yield a common positive field annihilated by the minimal and both null-expansion Jacobi operators.
- **C8** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-variation-jacobi-singular-ends)): Let $\Sigma$ be a connected regular component of the compact locally perimeter-minimizing boundary $\Gamma$. Every smooth positive solution of $$\Delta_\Sigma\varphi+ (\|A_\Sigma\|^2+\operatorname{Ric}_g(\nu,\nu))\varphi=0$$ satisfies $\inf_\Sigma\varphi>0$. Moreover, $\varphi(x_j)\to+\infty$ for every sequence $x_j\in\Sigma$ with $\operatorname{dist}(x_j,\mathcal S)\to0$.
  - Explanation: Positive Jacobi fields stay bounded below and diverge along every approach to the singular set, preventing escape of comparison maxima.
- **C9** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-variation-diffuse-bv-minima)): Let $f\geq0$ be locally Lipschitz on an interval $I$, and assume its almost-everywhere derivative $v=f'$ belongs to $BV_{\mathrm{loc}}(I)$. If $D^dv$ denotes the nonatomic part of $Dv$, then $$\|D^dv\|(\{f=0\})=0.$$
  - Explanation: The diffuse part of the second derivative of a nonnegative function does not charge its zero level.
- **C10** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-variation-boundary-support)): Under the rigidity hypotheses and equality, the probability measure in Proposition <a href="#prop:variation:multiplier" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:variation:multiplier">12</a> satisfies $$\pi\{C:\Gamma_C=S\}=1.$$ Consequently, on every compact variation and end prototype, $$\label{eq:variation:boundary-multiplier} 2k\omega\mathcal E'(h,p)-c a'_S(h) =\int_{\mathfrak A}\mathfrak C'(h,p;v)\,d\Lambda -\int_S\theta'_+(h,p)\,d\zeta, \qquad a'_S(h)=\frac12\int_S\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_Sh\,dA.$$ In particular the area source in Equation <a href="#eq:variation:hessian" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:variation:hessian">[eq:variation:hessian]</a> vanishes in the open exterior. Boundary mass of the constraint measure $\Lambda$ is not included in this conclusion.
  - Explanation: Under equality and rigidity, every area multiplier is carried by the original boundary. This does not yet remove boundary mass of the constraint measure.
- **C11** (classification, [source](#stmt-thm-static-classification)): Under the equality and rigidity hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#thm:rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:rigidity">5</a>, the original exterior, with its boundary included, admits a smooth spacelike embedding into the regular Schwarzschild–Tangherlini exterior of mass $m$. Its induced metric and future-normal second fundamental form are $g$ and $K$. The boundary is a full section of the future horizon, or the bifurcation sphere, and the end approaches spatial infinity.
  - Explanation: The localized adjoint system recovers the original hypersurface, its second fundamental form and its smooth horizon attachment.
- **C12** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-static-positive)): One has $W>0$ throughout $\operatorname{int}\Omega$. The static base metric $h=g+W^{-1}X^\flat\otimes X^\flat$ has a smooth one-sided attachment at $S$, with induced metric $g\|_{TS}$, and $$\label{eq:static:static-equations} \mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}_h\lambda=\lambda\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_h,\qquad \Delta_h\lambda=0,\qquad R_h=0,\qquad 0<\lambda<1,\quad \lambda=\sqrt W.$$ At the attached boundary $S$, $\|d\lambda\|_h=\kappa$ and the boundary is totally geodesic. The even reflection of $h$ and odd reflection of $\lambda$ are at least $C^{2,\alpha}$ for $0<\alpha<1$.
  - Explanation: The stationary norm is positive throughout the original interior, and the static base attaches smoothly with totally geodesic boundary.
- **C13** (classification, [source](#stmt-prop-static-euclidean-double)): The filled metric $(N,\gamma_*)$ of Lemma <a href="#lem:static:filled-double" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:static:filled-double">39</a> is isometric to Euclidean $\R^n$.
  - Explanation: The filled conformal double is globally Euclidean.
- **C14** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q-converse-lem-boost)): In the Schwarzschild–Tangherlini spacetime of geometric mass $M>0$, let $b,y$ be static time and isotropic spatial coordinates. Make the Lorentz change $$\label{q:converse:eq:boost-coordinates} b=\gamma(T+vx^1),\qquad y^1=\gamma(x^1+vT),\qquad y^a=x^a\ (2\le a\le n),\qquad \gamma=(1-v^2)^{-1/2},$$ where $0\le v<1$. The induced data on $T=0$, oriented by the future normal, have $$\label{q:converse:eq:boost-charges} E=\gamma M,\qquad P_1=\gamma Mv,\qquad P_a=0\ (a>1).$$ The metric and second fundamental form have the homogeneous leading terms computed below, with remainders $O_d(r^{-2p})$ and $O_d(r^{-2p-1})$, respectively, for every fixed derivative order $d$.
  - Explanation: The original ADM fluxes of a boosted model plane give the Lorentz-transformed energy and momentum.
- **C15** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q-converse-prop-adm)): Under the hypotheses of Lemma <a href="#q:converse:lem:plane" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q:converse:lem:plane">45</a>, the ADM limits of the original induced data exist and satisfy $$E=M u_\infty,\qquad P_i=-M\delta_{ij}X_\infty^j, \qquad E>0,\qquad E^2-\|P\|^2=M^2. \label{q:converse:eq:charges}$$ In particular the invariant mass is $M$. No parity assumption is needed.
  - Explanation: Admissible slice height and coordinate changes preserve the invariant ADM mass without a parity assumption.
- **C16** (construction, [source](#stmt-q-converse-prop-examples)): For every $n\ge3$ and every $M>0$, the static exterior slice satisfies all hypotheses of the rigidity subclass and realizes equality. There are also smooth examples with $K\not\equiv0$, obtained by nonconstant radial static-time graphs supported in any prescribed annulus strictly outside the horizon. These examples are vacuum, complete with their boundary included, have the same horizon and asymptotic end as the static slice, and satisfy $$\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_g(\Gamma)\ge\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_g(S) \quad\hbox{for every full enclosing cut }\Gamma.$$ They have no smooth compact weakly future-trapped enclosing hypersurface lying wholly in the interior.
  - Explanation: Static slices and compactly supported radial time graphs give admissible equality examples with the required full-cut area and outermostness properties.
- **C17** (classification, [source](#stmt-q3-intro-rigidity)): Let $(M,g,K)$ be a smooth connected orientable complete initial data set without boundary, consisting of a compact core and finitely many asymptotically flat ends. On each end assume $g-\delta=O_2(r^{-q})$, $K=O_1(r^{-1-q})$, with $q>1/2$, and existing finite ADM flux limits. Assume that $\mu$ and $\|J\|_g$ are integrable and that $\mu\geq\|J\|_g$ everywhere.* *Choose an end and a finite nonempty disjoint union $$S=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^{\ell}S_i,\qquad 1\leq\ell<\infty,$$ of compact connected smooth embedded two-sided surfaces without boundary, separating that end from a complementary region. Let $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$ be the closure of the connected side toward the chosen end. Suppose that $\partial M_{\mathrm{ext}}=S$, that $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$ has exactly this one end, and that, for the normal pointing into $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$:* 1. *every $S_i$ is a future MOTS, so $H_{S_i}+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{S_i}K=0$;* 2. *$S$ is outermost in the partial-coincidence sense of Definition <a href="#q3:rigidity:partial-outermostness" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q3:rigidity:partial-outermostness">52</a>;* 3. *every enclosing cut in the closed exterior has area at least $A=\|S\|_g=\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\|S_i\|_g>0$.* *Let $(E,P)$ be the ADM vector of the chosen end. If $$\label{q3:intro:equality} E>\|P\|_\delta,\qquad m=\sqrt{E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2}=\sqrt{\frac{A}{16\pi}},$$ then $\ell=1$ and $S$ is diffeomorphic to a sphere. There is a proper smooth spacelike embedding of the entire original $M_{\mathrm{ext}}$ into the maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime of mass $m$, inducing $g$ and the given $K$ for a consistent future unit normal. The chosen end approaches the corresponding spatial infinity. The image of $S$ is a smooth cross-section of the corresponding future horizon or the bifurcation sphere. The embedding and its future normal are smooth up to $S$, and the image extends as a smooth spacelike hypersurface through that boundary.
  - Explanation: Finite-component equality under partial-coincidence outermostness forces a single spherical horizon and a smooth original-data Schwarzschild embedding.
- **C18** (classification, [source](#stmt-q3-intro-connected-rigidity)): Under the ambient, asymptotic, and exterior hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#q3:intro:rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q3:intro:rigidity">53</a>, suppose that $S$ is connected. Retain conditions <span class="upright">(i)</span> and <span class="upright">(iii)</span>, and replace condition <span class="upright">(ii)</span> by the following weaker outermostness condition: there is no compact smooth embedded surface wholly contained in $\operatorname{Int}M_{\mathrm{ext}}$, possibly disconnected, separating $S$ from the distant end and having $\theta_+\le0$ everywhere for the normal toward that end. If <a href="#q3:intro:equality" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q3:intro:equality">[q3:intro:equality]</a> holds with $A=\|S\|_g$, then $S$ is diffeomorphic to a sphere and all the original-data Schwarzschild embedding conclusions of Theorem <a href="#q3:intro:rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q3:intro:rigidity">53</a> hold.
  - Explanation: For connected boundary, excluding wholly interior weakly trapped enclosing surfaces suffices for the Schwarzschild conclusion.
- **C19** (bound, [source](#stmt-q3-rigidity-finite-strictness)): Under the hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#q3:intro:rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q3:intro:rigidity">53</a>, retain $E>\|P\|_\delta$ but do not assume its equality in mass and area. If $\ell\geq2$, then $$\sqrt{E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2}>\sqrt{\frac{A}{16\pi}}.$$
  - Explanation: Disconnected boundary implies qualitative strictness under the finite-component theorem hypotheses.
- **C20** (bound, [source](#stmt-q3-local-spinor-strictness)): Let $(M,g,K)$ be smooth connected orientable three-dimensional initial data without boundary, with $g$ complete and with finitely many asymptotically flat ends outside a compact set. Assume on every end $$g-\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\qquad K=O_1(r^{-1-q}),\qquad q>\tfrac12,$$ integrable constraint densities $\mu,\|J\|_g$, finite ADM charges, and $\mu\geq \|J\|_g$ everywhere. Here $16\pi\mu=R_g+(\operatorname{tr}_gK)^2-\|K\|_g^2$ and $8\pi J=\operatorname{div}_g(K-(\operatorname{tr}_gK)g)$. Let $S_1,S_2$ be disjoint smooth embedded two-sided spheres, and suppose that the closure $\Omega$ of the connected exterior toward a designated end has boundary $S=S_1\sqcup S_2$ and exactly that one end.* *Orient $S$ into $\Omega$. Assume $\theta_+=H+\operatorname{tr}_S K=0$ on $S$, and assume every full enclosing cut has area at least $A=\|S_1\|_g+\|S_2\|_g$. A full cut is the entire compact smooth frontier of a connected end-containing outer domain, with all components and coincident portions of $S$ counted and bounded complementary pockets filled. Finally assume there is no such cut $\Gamma\ne S$ whose components either equal an $S_i$ or lie wholly in the open exterior, with at least one component in the open exterior and $\theta_+(\Gamma)\leq0$ toward the designated end. If that end has $E>\|P\|_\delta$, then $$\sqrt{E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2} >\sqrt{\frac{\|S_1\|_g+\|S_2\|_g}{16\pi}}.$$
  - Explanation: A local spinor argument excludes equality for the stated exterior with disjoint spherical horizon components.
- **C21** (bound, [source](#stmt-q4-thm-numerical-provider)): Suppose $(\Omega,g,K)$ satisfies the smoothness, orientability, completeness, end, integrability, decay, and finite-charge assumptions above, as well as $\mu\ge\|J\|_g$ and $\theta_+\le0$ on every component of its nonempty compact boundary. Then $A_*(g)>0$ and $$\label{q4:eq:numerical} E\ge\sqrt{\|P\|_\delta^2+\frac14 \left(\frac{A_*(g)}\omega\right)^{4/3}}.$$ In particular $E>\|P\|_\delta$ and $\sqrt{E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2}\ge\frac12(A_*(g)/\omega)^{2/3}$.
  - Explanation: The weak four-dimensional comparison supplies the inequality for variations without imposing the additional equality-class hypotheses.
- **C22** (classification, [source](#stmt-q4-thm-rigidity)): Let $(\Omega,g,K)$ belong to Definition <a href="#q4:def:horizon" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4:def:horizon">81</a>, and set $m=\sqrt{E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2}$. Then $$\label{q4:eq:intro-equality} m=\frac12\left(\frac A\omega\right)^{2/3}$$ if and only if the original initial data admit a global smooth spacelike embedding, including $S$, into the regular maximal extension of $\overline g_m$. The image lies in the closure of the corresponding exterior, its end approaches that spatial infinity, and $S$ maps to a smooth section of its future horizon or to its bifurcation sphere. The induced metric is the original $g$, and its second fundamental form for a consistent future unit normal is the original $K$ with convention <a href="#q4:eq:intro-second-fundamental-form" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q4:eq:intro-second-fundamental-form">[q4:eq:intro-second-fundamental-form]</a>. The embedding and normal are smooth up to $S$ in regular horizon coordinates.* *Equivalently, every such hypersurface in $\overline g_{M_0}$ satisfying Definition <a href="#q4:def:horizon" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4:def:horizon">81</a> and the prescribed asymptotic assumptions has invariant ADM mass $M_0$, horizon area $\omega(2M_0)^{3/2}$, and equality in <a href="#q4:eq:numerical" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="q4:eq:numerical">[q4:eq:numerical]</a>.
  - Explanation: Under the connected outermost horizon hypotheses, equality is equivalent to a smooth original-data Tangherlini embedding with regular horizon attachment.
- **C23** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4-var-area-localization)): For $\varpi$-almost every element of $\mathcal T$, its frontier equals $S$, where $\varpi$ is the measure in Proposition <a href="#q4:var:multiplier" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4:var:multiplier">91</a>. Consequently, for every variation $H=(h,p)$ in $\mathcal V$, $$\int_{\mathcal T}a'_T(h)\,\,\mathrm d\varpi(T) =a'_S(h)=\tfrac12\int_S\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_S h\,\,\mathrm dA_g. \label{q4:var:localized-area}$$ In particular the multiplier identity becomes $$6\omega\mathcal E'(H)-c\,a'_S(h) =\langle C'_H,\Lambda\rangle -\int_S\theta'_H\,\,\mathrm d\eta+za. \label{q4:var:localized-identity}$$
  - Explanation: Normal tests and outermostness concentrate the minimizing-frontier multiplier on the horizon.
- **C24** (construction, [source](#stmt-q4-adj-causal-field)): There are a smooth function $u$ and a smooth vector field $X$ on $\Omega$, smooth up to its one-sided boundary, with the following properties.* 1. *They satisfy $u\ge \|X\|_g$, $u>0$ in $\operatorname{int}\Omega$, and $$u\mu+J(X)=0. \label{q4:adj:complementarity}$$ With symmetric indices denoting averaging, their equations are $$\begin{aligned} \nabla_{(i}X_{j)}&=-uK_{ij}, \label{q4:adj:kid-first}\\ \Delta u&=-\operatorname{div}_g\bigl(K(X,\cdot)^\sharp\bigr), \label{q4:adj:conformal-adjoint}\\ \nabla^2u &=u(\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_g+\tau K-2K^2)-\mathcal L_XK+X_{(i}J_{j)}. \label{q4:adj:kid-second} \end{aligned}$$ Here $X_i=g_{ij}X^j$ and $(K^2)_{ij}=K_{ik}K^k{}_j$.* 2. *On the chosen asymptotically flat end, $$(u,X)=(b^0,b)+O_2(r^{-q_0}). \label{q4:adj:decay}$$* 3. *At the boundary, for the unit normal $\nu$ pointing into $\Omega$, $$X=u\nu,\qquad \partial_\nu u+K(X,\nu)=\kappa. \label{q4:adj:horizon-data}$$ Either $u>0$ everywhere on $S$ or $u=0$ everywhere on $S$.* 4. *On $\mathbb R\times\operatorname{int}\Omega$, set $$\mathbf g=-u^2\,\mathrm dt^2 +g_{ij}(\mathrm dx^i+X^i\,\mathrm dt) (\mathrm dx^j+X^j\,\mathrm dt), \qquad \xi=\partial_t,\qquad N=u^2-\|X\|_g^2. \label{q4:adj:stationary-metric}$$ For the future normal $n=u^{-1}(\xi-X)$, the slice $t=0$ has exactly the original induced metric $g$ and second fundamental form $K$, with the convention of Theorem <a href="#q4:thm:rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4:thm:rigidity">82</a>. Moreover, $$\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_{\mathbf g}(\xi,\cdot)=0, \qquad \mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_{\mathbf g}=0\quad\hbox{on }\{N>0\}. \label{q4:adj:ricci}$$* 5. *We have $N\ge0$, $N\to1$ at infinity, and $N>0$ in a full collar just outside $S$. More precisely, in the positive boundary-lapse case, $$N\|_S=0,\qquad \mathrm dN\|_S=2u\kappa\,\nu^\flat=2\kappa X^\flat. \label{q4:adj:positive-collar}$$ In the zero boundary-lapse case, if $s\ge0$ is the original $g$-normal distance from $S$, there are smooth one-sided fields $d,Y_2$ such that $$u=sd,\qquad X=s^2Y_2,\qquad d\|_S=\kappa,\qquad N=s^2\bigl(d^2-s^2\|Y_2\|_g^2\bigr). \label{q4:adj:zero-collar}$$ Consequently all zeros of $N$ in $\operatorname{int}\Omega$ lie in a compact subset of that interior.
  - Explanation: The localized multipliers yield smooth causal lapse and shift fields on the original one-sided exterior.
- **C25** (classification, [source](#stmt-q4-cla-static-classification)): The positive component is the whole original open exterior: $\mathcal U=\operatorname{int}\Omega$ and $N>0$ there. Its attached boundary is $S$. There is a global isometry of the static base onto the Schwarzschild–Tangherlini spatial exterior of mass $m$, under which $$\label{q4:cla:ST-base} h_b=\left(1+\frac{m}{2\rho^2}\right)^2 (\,\mathrm d\rho^2+\rho^2 g_{\mathbb S^3}),\qquad \lambda=\frac{1-m/(2\rho^2)}{1+m/(2\rho^2)}, \qquad \rho\ge\sqrt{m/2}.$$ The isometry is smooth on the open base and in its one-sided regular boundary structure. The attachment is homeomorphic to the original attachment of $S$ in $\Omega$ and restricts smoothly on $S$. In particular the open base is simply connected and $S$ is a round three-sphere in its induced metric. The base reflection is smooth in signed $\lambda$ in the positive boundary-lapse case; its angular coordinates can be taken constant along base normal geodesics.
  - Explanation: The positive stationary component is the whole original interior and its static base is the Schwarzschild–Tangherlini spatial exterior.
- **C26** (classification, [source](#stmt-q4-rec-embedding)): Equality under the horizon hypotheses gives a global smooth spacelike embedding of the original $\Omega$, including $S$, in the regular maximal Tangherlini extension of mass $m$. The embedding pulls back the spacetime metric and the future second fundamental form to the original $g$ and $K$. Its image lies in the closure of the corresponding exterior, its boundary has the form stated in Lemma <a href="#q4:rec:horizon-extension" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4:rec:horizon-extension">109</a>, and its end approaches the corresponding spatial infinity.
  - Explanation: Reconstruction gives a global spacelike embedding that pulls back to the original metric and future second fundamental form.
- **C27** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4-rec-converse-mass)): Every hypersurface in the converse class of Theorem <a href="#q4:thm:rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4:thm:rigidity">82</a>, in Tangherlini spacetime of geometric mass $M_0>0$, has invariant ADM mass $M_0$. More precisely, in coordinates adapted to its asymptotic boost, its charges are $E=M_0\Gamma$ and $P=M_0\Gamma v\,e_1$, where $0\leq v<1$ and $\Gamma=(1-v^2)^{-1/2}$.
  - Explanation: Every hypersurface in the stated converse class has invariant ADM mass equal to the background geometric mass.
- **C28** (theorem, [source](#stmt-q4-rec-horizon-area)): A smooth spacelike section of a future Tangherlini horizon of geometric mass $M_0>0$, including its bifurcation sphere, has induced metric $(2M_0)g_{\mathbb S^3}$ and three-volume $\omega(2M_0)^{3/2}$.
  - Explanation: A smooth horizon section has the round induced metric and the prescribed horizon three-volume.

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-thm-converse",
        "exact_quote": "Let $M>0$. Every smooth spacelike exterior hypersurface in the regular extension of $\\mathbf G_M$, with its interior in $r>r_M$, whose induced data satisfy Definitions <a href=\"#def:data\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"def:data\">1</a>, <a href=\"#def:fullcuts\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"def:fullcuts\">2</a>, and <a href=\"#def:setting:rigidity\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"def:setting:rigidity\">4</a>, whose boundary is a full smooth section of the corresponding future horizon or its bifurcation sphere, and whose end approaches spatial infinity, has $$(E^2-|P|_\\delta^2)^{1/2}=M,\\qquad\n A=\\omega(2M)^{\\frac{n-1}{n-2}}.\n \\label{eq:setting:converse}$$ It therefore attains equality in <a href=\"#eq:setting:main\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:setting:main\">[eq:setting:main]</a>.     {
      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-q-geometry-enclosure",
        "exact_quote": "The minimum in Equation <a href=\"#q:geometry:full-perimeter\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"q:geometry:full-perimeter\">[q:geometry:full-perimeter]</a> exists, equals $a(g)>0$, and is independent of the filling. All its minimizing sets are contained in one compact region. Their multiplicity-one frontiers are smooth minimal hypersurfaces away from $B$ and a singular set of Hausdorff dimension at most $n-8$; the singular set is empty when $n\\le7$. Every contact point with $B$ is regular, with a $C^{1,\\alpha}\\cap W^{2,p}$ graph for every finite $p$ and $0<\\alpha<1$. For $n=3,4$ the whole frontier is $C^{1,1}$, including contact, and its graph functions are $W^{2,\\infty}$.*\n\n*In dimensions $3$ and $4$, each frontier bounds a connected exterior and is the $C^1$ and area limit of smooth full cuts contained in $\\operatorname{int}X$. If $H_B<0$ for the normal into $X$, every minimizer contains one fixed exterior collar of $B$. In dimensions $3$ and $4$ its frontier is then a smooth minimal full cut; its closed exterior is connected, one-ended, complete with its boundary included, and outer area-minimizing with all boundary components counted. In every dimension, whenever a minimizing frontier is smooth, its closed exterior has these same connectedness, completeness, one-end and outer area-minimization properties.",

    {
      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-q-geometry-envelope",
        "exact_quote": "The space $\\mathcal T(g)$ is compact and metrizable. For every smooth symmetric two-tensor $h$ the function $$E\\longmapsto a'_E(h):=\n \\frac12\\int_{\\partial^*E}\\operatorname{tr}_{T\\partial^*E}h\\,dA_g$$ is continuous on it. Let $g_t$, $|t|<t_0$, be a smooth path of smooth metrics with $g_0=g$, extended smoothly through the fixed boundary. Assume uniform comparison with $g$, and bounded first and second parameter derivatives relative to $g$. One sufficient end hypothesis is $$\\label{q:geometry:uniform-AF}\n g_t-\\delta=O_2(r^{-q_*})\\quad\\hbox{uniformly for }|t|<t_0,\n \\qquad q_*>0.$$ More generally, it suffices that the coordinate spheres have positive outward mean curvature beyond one common radius. The result also holds if the end metrics are uniformly comparable to the Euclidean metric with uniform scaled $C^1$ bounds; they need not have a common mean-convex tail in this last alternative. Put $h=\\partial_tg_t|_0$. Then $$\\label{q:geometry:envelope-derivative}\n \\left.\\frac{d}{dt}\\right|_{0+}a(g_t)\n       =\\min_{E\\in\\mathcal T(g)}a'_E(h).$$ For any $t_j\\to0$ and any $E_j\\in\\mathcal T(g_{t_j})$, a subsequence converges in $L^1$ to $E\\in\\mathcal T(g)$, with convergence of perimeters and of the plane measures computed in the fixed metric $g$.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.11"
      },

Let $g_t$, $|t|<t_0$, be a smooth path of smooth metrics with $g_0=g$, extended smoothly through the fixed boundary. Assume uniform comparison with $g$, and bounded first and second parameter derivatives relative to $g$. One sufficient end hypothesis is $$\\label{q:geometry:uniform-AF}\n g_t-\\delta=O_2(r^{-q_*})\\quad\\hbox{uniformly for }|t|<t_0,\n \\qquad q_*>0.$$ More generally, it suffices that the coordinate spheres have positive outward mean curvature beyond one common radius. The result also holds if the end metrics are uniformly comparable to the Euclidean metric with uniform scaled $C^1$ bounds; they need not have a common mean-convex tail in this last alternative. Put $h=\\partial_tg_t|_0$. Then $$\\label{q:geometry:envelope-derivative}\n \\left.\\frac{d}{dt}\\right|_{0+}a(g_t)\n       =\\min_{E\\in\\mathcal T(g)}a'_E(h).$$ For any $t_j\\to0$ and any $E_j\\in\\mathcal T(g_{t_j})$, a subsequence converges in $L^1$ to $E\\in\\mathcal T(g)$, with convergence of perimeters and of the plane measures computed in the fixed metric $g$.",
          "source_id": "PM-260.11"
        }
      ],
      "statement_anchor": "stmt-q-geometry-envelope"
    },

        "exact_quote": "In the Schwarzschild–Tangherlini spacetime of geometric mass $M>0$, let $b,y$ be static time and isotropic spatial coordinates.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-q-converse-prop-examples",
        "exact_quote": "For every $n\\ge3$ and every $M>0$, the static exterior slice satisfies all hypotheses of the rigidity subclass and realizes equality. There are also smooth examples with $K\\not\\equiv0$, obtained by nonconstant radial static-time graphs supported in any prescribed annulus strictly outside the horizon. These examples are vacuum, complete with their boundary included, have the same horizon and asymptotic end as the static slice, and satisfy $$\\mathop{\\mathrm{Area}}_g(\\Gamma)\\ge\\mathop{\\mathrm{Area}}_g(S)\n \\quad\\hbox{for every full enclosing cut }\\Gamma.$$ They have no smooth compact weakly future-trapped enclosing hypersurface lying wholly in the interior.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.11"
      },

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-q3-intro-rigidity",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(M,g,K)$ be a smooth connected orientable complete initial data set without boundary, consisting of a compact core and finitely many asymptotically flat ends. On each end assume $g-\\delta=O_2(r^{-q})$, $K=O_1(r^{-1-q})$, with $q>1/2$, and existing finite ADM flux limits. Assume that $\\mu$ and $|J|_g$ are integrable and that $\\mu\\geq|J|_g$ everywhere.*\n\n*Choose an end and a finite nonempty disjoint union $$S=\\bigsqcup_{i=1}^{\\ell}S_i,\\qquad 1\\leq\\ell<\\infty,$$ of compact connected smooth embedded two-sided surfaces without boundary, separating that end from a complementary region. Let $M_{\\mathrm{ext}}$ be the closure of the connected side toward the chosen end. Suppose that $\\partial M_{\\mathrm{ext}}=S$, that $M_{\\mathrm{ext}}$ has exactly this one end, and that, for the normal pointing into $M_{\\mathrm{ext}}$:*\n\n1.  *every $S_i$ is a future MOTS, so $H_{S_i}+\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_{S_i}K=0$;*\n\n2.  *$S$ is outermost in the partial-coincidence sense of Definition <a href=\"#q3:rigidity:partial-outermostness\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"q3:rigidity:partial-outermostness\">52</a>;*\n\n3.  *every enclosing cut in the closed exterior has area at least $A=|S|_g=\\sum_{i=1}^{\\ell}|S_i|_g>0$.*\n\n\n*Let $(E,P)$ be the ADM vector of the chosen end. If $$\\label{q3:intro:equality}\nE>|P|_\\delta,\\qquad\nm=\\sqrt{E^2-|P|_\\delta^2}=\\sqrt{\\frac{A}{16\\pi}},$$ then $\\ell=1$ and $S$ is diffeomorphic to a sphere. There is a proper smooth spacelike embedding of the entire original $M_{\\mathrm{ext}}$ into the maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime of mass $m$, inducing $g$ and the given $K$ for a consistent future unit normal. The chosen end approaches the corresponding spatial infinity. The image of $S$ is a smooth cross-section of the corresponding future horizon or the bifurcation sphere. The embedding and its future normal are smooth up to $S$, and the image extends as a smooth spacelike hypersurface through that boundary.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.11"
      },

Suppose that $\\partial M_{\\mathrm{ext}}=S$, that $M_{\\mathrm{ext}}$ has exactly this one end, and that, for the normal pointing into $M_{\\mathrm{ext}}$:*\n\n1.  *every $S_i$ is a future MOTS, so $H_{S_i}+\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_{S_i}K=0$;*\n\n2.  *$S$ is outermost in the partial-coincidence sense of Definition <a href=\"#q3:rigidity:partial-outermostness\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"q3:rigidity:partial-outermostness\">52</a>;*\n\n3.  *every enclosing cut in the closed exterior has area at least $A=|S|_g=\\sum_{i=1}^{\\ell}|S_i|_g>0$.*\n\n\n*Let $(E,P)$ be the ADM vector of the chosen end. If $$\\label{q3:intro:equality}\nE>|P|_\\delta,\\qquad\nm=\\sqrt{E^2-|P|_\\delta^2}=\\sqrt{\\frac{A}{16\\pi}},$$ then $\\ell=1$ and $S$ is diffeomorphic to a sphere. There is a proper smooth spacelike embedding of the entire original $M_{\\mathrm{ext}}$ into the maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime of mass $m$, inducing $g$ and the given $K$ for a consistent future unit normal. The chosen end approaches the corresponding spatial infinity. The image of $S$ is a smooth cross-section of the corresponding future horizon or the bifurcation sphere. The embedding and its future normal are smooth up to $S$, and the image extends as a smooth spacelike hypersurface through that boundary.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-q3-local-spinor-strictness",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(M,g,K)$ be smooth connected orientable three-dimensional initial data without boundary, with $g$ complete and with finitely many asymptotically flat ends outside a compact set. Assume on every end $$g-\\delta=O_2(r^{-q}),\\qquad K=O_1(r^{-1-q}),\\qquad q>\\tfrac12,$$ integrable constraint densities $\\mu,|J|_g$, finite ADM charges, and $\\mu\\geq |J|_g$ everywhere. Here $16\\pi\\mu=R_g+(\\operatorname{tr}_gK)^2-|K|_g^2$ and $8\\pi J=\\operatorname{div}_g(K-(\\operatorname{tr}_gK)g)$. Let $S_1,S_2$ be disjoint smooth embedded two-sided spheres, and suppose that the closure $\\Omega$ of the connected exterior toward a designated end has boundary $S=S_1\\sqcup S_2$ and exactly that one end.*\n\n*Orient $S$ into $\\Omega$. Assume $\\theta_+=H+\\operatorname{tr}_S K=0$ on $S$, and assume every full enclosing cut has area at least $A=|S_1|_g+|S_2|_g$. A full cut is the entire compact smooth frontier of a connected end-containing outer domain, with all components and coincident portions of $S$ counted and bounded complementary pockets filled. Finally assume there is no such cut $\\Gamma\\ne S$ whose components either equal an $S_i$ or lie wholly in the open exterior, with at least one component in the open exterior and $\\theta_+(\\Gamma)\\leq0$ toward the designated end. If that end has $E>|P|_\\delta$, then $$\\sqrt{E^2-|P|_\\delta^2}\n    >\\sqrt{\\frac{|S_1|_g+|S_2|_g}{16\\pi}}.$$",

        "exact_quote": "Let $(\\Omega,g,K)$ belong to Definition <a href=\"#q4:def:horizon\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"q4:def:horizon\">81</a>, and set $m=\\sqrt{E^2-|P|_\\delta^2}$. Then $$\\label{q4:eq:intro-equality}\n m=\\frac12\\left(\\frac A\\omega\\right)^{2/3}$$ if and only if the original initial data admit a global smooth spacelike embedding, including $S$, into the regular maximal extension of $\\overline g_m$. The induced metric is the original $g$, and its second fundamental form for a consistent future unit normal is the original $K$ with convention <a href=\"#q4:eq:intro-second-fundamental-form\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"q4:eq:intro-second-fundamental-form\">[q4:eq:intro-second-fundamental-form]</a>.       "exact_statement": "Let $(\\Omega,g,K)$ belong to Definition <a href=\"#q4:def:horizon\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"q4:def:horizon\">81</a>, and set $m=\\sqrt{E^2-|P|_\\delta^2}$. Then $$\\label{q4:eq:intro-equality}\n m=\\frac12\\left(\\frac A\\omega\\right)^{2/3}$$ if and only if the original initial data admit a global smooth spacelike embedding, including $S$, into the regular maximal extension of $\\overline g_m$. The image lies in the closure of the corresponding exterior, its end approaches that spatial infinity, and $S$ maps to a smooth section of its future horizon or to its bifurcation sphere. The induced metric is the original $g$, and its second fundamental form for a consistent future unit normal is the original $K$ with convention <a href=\"#q4:eq:intro-second-fundamental-form\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"q4:eq:intro-second-fundamental-form\">[q4:eq:intro-second-fundamental-form]</a>. The embedding and normal are smooth up to $S$ in regular horizon coordinates.*\n\n*Equivalently, every such hypersurface in $\\overline g_{M_0}$ satisfying Definition <a href=\"#q4:def:horizon\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"q4:def:horizon\">81</a> and the prescribed asymptotic assumptions has invariant ADM mass $M_0$, horizon area $\\omega(2M_0)^{3/2}$, and equality in <a href=\"#q4:eq:numerical\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"q4:eq:numerical\">[q4:eq:numerical]</a>.",
      "explanation": "Under the connected outermost horizon hypotheses, equality is equivalent to a smooth original-data Tangherlini embedding with regular horizon attachment.",
      "fidelity": "PENDING",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-q4-var-area-localization",
        "exact_quote": "For $\\varpi$-almost every element of $\\mathcal T$, its frontier equals $S$, where $\\varpi$ is the measure in Proposition <a href=\"#q4:var:multiplier\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"q4:var:multiplier\">91</a>. Consequently, for every variation $H=(h,p)$ in $\\mathcal V$, $$\\int_{\\mathcal T}a'_T(h)\\,\\,\\mathrm d\\varpi(T)\n       =a'_S(h)=\\tfrac12\\int_S\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_S h\\,\\,\\mathrm dA_g.\n\\label{q4:var:localized-area}$$ In particular the multiplier identity becomes $$6\\omega\\mathcal E'(H)-c\\,a'_S(h)\n  =\\langle C'_H,\\Lambda\\rangle\n       -\\int_S\\theta'_H\\,\\,\\mathrm d\\eta+za.\n\\label{q4:var:localized-identity}$$",
        "source_id": "PM-260.11"
      },

    {
      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-q4-adj-causal-field",
        "exact_quote": "There are a smooth function $u$ and a smooth vector field $X$ on $\\Omega$, smooth up to its one-sided boundary, with the following properties.*\n\n\n\n\n\n1.  *They satisfy $u\\ge |X|_g$, $u>0$ in $\\operatorname{int}\\Omega$, and $$u\\mu+J(X)=0.\n     \\label{q4:adj:complementarity}$$ With symmetric indices denoting averaging, their equations are $$\\begin{aligned}\n     \\nabla_{(i}X_{j)}&=-uK_{ij},\n     \\label{q4:adj:kid-first}\\\\\n     \\Delta u&=-\\operatorname{div}_g\\bigl(K(X,\\cdot)^\\sharp\\bigr),\n     \\label{q4:adj:conformal-adjoint}\\\\\n     \\nabla^2u\n     &=u(\\mathop{\\mathrm{Ric}}_g+\\tau K-2K^2)-\\mathcal L_XK+X_{(i}J_{j)}.\n     \\label{q4:adj:kid-second}\n    \\end{aligned}$$ Here $X_i=g_{ij}X^j$ and $(K^2)_{ij}=K_{ik}K^k{}_j$.*\n\n\n2.  *On the chosen asymptotically flat end, $$(u,X)=(b^0,b)+O_2(r^{-q_0}).\n     \\label{q4:adj:decay}$$*\n\n\n3.  *At the boundary, for the unit normal $\\nu$ pointing into $\\Omega$, $$X=u\\nu,\\qquad\n     \\partial_\\nu u+K(X,\\nu)=\\kappa.\n     \\label{q4:adj:horizon-data}$$ Either $u>0$ everywhere on $S$ or $u=0$ everywhere on $S$.*\n\n\n\n4.  *On $\\mathbb R\\times\\operatorname{int}\\Omega$, set $$\\mathbf g=-u^2\\,\\mathrm dt^2\n       +g_{ij}(\\mathrm dx^i+X^i\\,\\mathrm dt)\n              (\\mathrm dx^j+X^j\\,\\mathrm dt),\n     \\qquad \\xi=\\partial_t,\\qquad N=u^2-|X|_g^2.\n     \\label{q4:adj:stationary-metric}$$ For the future normal $n=u^{-1}(\\xi-X)$, the slice $t=0$ has exactly the original induced metric $g$ and second fundamental form $K$, with the convention of Theorem <a href=\"#q4:thm:rigidity\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"q4:thm:rigidity\">82</a>. Moreover, $$\\mathop{\\mathrm{Ric}}_{\\mathbf g}(\\xi,\\cdot)=0,\n     \\qquad \\mathop{\\mathrm{Ric}}_{\\mathbf g}=0\\quad\\hbox{on }\\{N>0\\}.\n     \\label{q4:adj:ricci}$$*\n\n\n\n5.  *We have $N\\ge0$, $N\\to1$ at infinity, and $N>0$ in a full collar just outside $S$. More precisely, in the positive boundary-lapse case, $$N|_S=0,\\qquad\n     \\mathrm dN|_S=2u\\kappa\\,\\nu^\\flat=2\\kappa X^\\flat.\n     \\label{q4:adj:positive-collar}$$ In the zero boundary-lapse case, if $s\\ge0$ is the original $g$-normal distance from $S$, there are smooth one-sided fields $d,Y_2$ such that $$u=sd,\\qquad X=s^2Y_2,\\qquad d|_S=\\kappa,\\qquad\n     N=s^2\\bigl(d^2-s^2|Y_2|_g^2\\bigr).\n     \\label{q4:adj:zero-collar}$$ Consequently all zeros of $N$ in $\\operatorname{int}\\Omega$ lie in a compact subset of that interior.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.11"
      },

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **One-ended initial-data exterior** ([source](#stmt-def-data)): A one-ended initial-data exterior is a smooth connected orientable $n$-manifold $\Omega$ with nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$, a smooth Riemannian metric $g$, and a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor $K$, both smooth up to $S$, satisfying the following conditions. The metric space $(\Omega,g)$, with $S$ included, is complete. There is a compact subset $C\subset\Omega$ such that $\Omega\setminus C$ is a single coordinate end diffeomorphic to $\{x\in\R^n:\|x\|>R_0\}$. In these coordinates, for some $$\frac{n-2}{2}<q<n-2,$$ we have $$g_{ij}-\delta_{ij}=O_6(r^{-q}),\qquad K_{ij}=O_5(r^{-1-q}),\qquad r=\|x\|. \label{eq:setting:decay}$$ Here $O_j(r^{-a})$ includes the estimate $\|\partial^\alpha T\|\le C_\alpha r^{-a-\|\alpha\|}$ for every $\|\alpha\|\le j$. These are asymptotic bounds on otherwise smooth data. Put $$\tau=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK,\qquad 2\mu=R_g+\tau^2-\|K\|_g^2,\qquad J_i=\nabla^j(K_{ij}-\tau g_{ij}). \label{eq:setting:constraints}$$ We assume the dominant energy condition and integrability: $$\mu\ge \|J\|_g,\qquad \mu,\ \|J\|_g\in L^1(\Omega,dV_g). \label{eq:setting:dec}$$ The ADM limits $$\begin{aligned} E&=\frac{1}{2k\omega} \lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{S_R} (\partial_jg_{ij}-\partial_ig_{jj})\,n_\delta^i\,dA_\delta, \label{eq:setting:energy}\\ P_i&=\frac{1}{k\omega} \lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{S_R} (K_{ij}-\tau g_{ij})\,n_\delta^j\,dA_\delta \label{eq:setting:momentum} \end{aligned}$$ exist and are finite. We impose the future-timelike condition $$E>\|P\|_\delta,\qquad m=(E^2-\|P\|_\delta^2)^{1/2}. \label{eq:setting:timelike}$$ On every component of $S$, the unit normal $\nu$ points into $\Omega$. We require $$\theta_+(S)=H_S+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_SK\le0,\qquad H_S=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_S\nu,\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_SK=(g^{ij}-\nu^i\nu^j)K_{ij}. \label{eq:setting:trapping}$$ There is no assumption on the other null expansion.
- **Full enclosing cut** ([source](#stmt-def-fullcuts)): A full enclosing cut is $\Gamma=\partial D$, the entire intrinsic manifold boundary of a connected smooth codimension-zero submanifold-with-boundary $D$ of $\Omega$, such that $D$ is closed in $\Omega$, its manifold interior lies in $\operatorname{int}\Omega$, and it contains the whole sufficiently distant coordinate end. We require $\Gamma$ to be compact, smooth, embedded, and two-sided. All components of $\partial D$ are counted, including any portion coincident with $S$. In particular, $D=\Omega$ is admissible and has full boundary $S$. Define $$A_{\min}(S)=\inf_{\Gamma}\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_g(\Gamma), \label{eq:setting:minarea}$$ and assume $A_{\min}(S)>0$.
- **Rigidity class** ([source](#stmt-def-setting-rigidity)): An exterior in Definition <a href="#def:data" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:data">1</a> belongs to the rigidity class if $S$ is connected, $\theta_+(S)=0$, every full cut has area at least $A=\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_g(S)>0$, and no compact smooth embedded two-sided enclosing hypersurface entirely in $\operatorname{int}\Omega$, possibly disconnected, has $\theta_+\le0$ everywhere with normal toward the end.
- **Three-dimensional exterior and enclosing area** ([source](#stmt-q3-intro-exterior-class)): An exterior is a connected orientable smooth three-manifold $\Omega$ with nonempty compact smooth boundary, complete as a metric space with its boundary included, and with exactly one end, which is asymptotically flat. An enclosing cut is a compact smooth embedded surface in $\overline\Omega$ separating the entire inner boundary from the sufficiently distant part of that end. Equivalently, it bounds the side containing the distant end; the other side is filled up to the inner obstacle. A cut may have several components and may coincide with the inner boundary. Its normal points toward the end. We put $$a_g(\partial\Omega)= \inf\{\|\Gamma\|_g:\Gamma\text{ is an enclosing cut}\}.$$ When using perimeter compactness, we take the closure of this class among filled inner sets and include the area of any frontier coinciding with the obstacle. Smooth outward approximation gives the same infimum. Enclosing cuts and minimizing sets are taken with bounded complementary pockets filled. Auxiliary perimeter arguments may use competitors containing the inner obstacle before filling: filling a bounded pocket deletes its frontier, cannot increase perimeter, and leaves the enclosing infimum unchanged.
- **Partial-coincidence outermostness** ([source](#stmt-q3-rigidity-partial-outermostness)): Let the boundary of a one-ended exterior be $S=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^{\ell}S_i$, with $1\leq\ell<\infty$ and each $S_i$ connected. The boundary is outermost in the partial-coincidence sense if no enclosing cut $\Gamma\ne S$ has all of the following properties: every connected component of $\Gamma$ is either an entire original component $S_i$ or is wholly contained in the open exterior; at least one component lies in the open exterior; and $\theta_+(\Gamma)\leq0$ everywhere for the normal toward the end.
- **Four-dimensional full enclosing cut** ([source](#stmt-q4-def-cuts)): A full enclosing cut is the entire intrinsic manifold boundary of a connected smooth codimension-zero submanifold $D\subset\Omega$, closed in $\Omega$, with compact boundary and with its manifold interior in $\operatorname{int}\Omega$, that contains the whole sufficiently distant end. Define $$A_*(g)=\inf_D\|\partial_{\mathrm{man}}D\|_g.$$ The cut may be disconnected, and every part coincident with $S$ is counted. In particular $D=\Omega$ is allowed and has full cut $S$. The infimum is not assumed attained by a smooth cut.
- **Connected outermost horizon** ([source](#stmt-q4-def-horizon)): The data satisfy all hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#q4:thm:numerical-provider" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4:thm:numerical-provider">80</a>, have connected boundary $S$, and satisfy the following additional conditions: 1. $S$ is a future marginally outer trapped surface (MOTS): $\theta_+(S)=0$ for the normal into $\Omega$. 2. No smooth compact embedded two-sided enclosing hypersurface in $\operatorname{int}\Omega$, possibly disconnected and oriented toward the end, has $\theta_+\le0$ everywhere. 3. $S$ is outer area-minimizing: every full cut has area at least $A:=\|S\|_g>0$. Thus $A_*(g)=A$.

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **R1** [claim](#stmt-q-geometry-enclosure) / [proof](#proof-stmt-q-geometry-enclosure): Direct perimeter minimization and obstacle regularity. -> Compact minimizing frontiers.
- **R2** [claim](#stmt-q-geometry-envelope) / [proof](#proof-stmt-q-geometry-envelope): Compactness of filled sets and continuity of tangent-plane measures. -> Right derivative of the enclosing-area envelope.
- **R3** [claim](#stmt-prop-variation-multiplier) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-variation-multiplier): Positive separation of feasible variations with active constraints. -> Causal complementary multiplier measures.
- **R4** [claim](#stmt-lem-variation-common-jacobi) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-variation-common-jacobi): Normalize neighboring sheets and pass to a positive Jacobi limit. -> Common positive Jacobi field.
- **R5** [claim](#stmt-lem-variation-jacobi-singular-ends) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-variation-jacobi-singular-ends): Capacity estimates, tangent-cone limits and the cone Liouville argument. -> Control at every singular end.
- **R6** [claim](#stmt-thm-variation-boundary-support) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-variation-boundary-support): Atomic flatness, diffuse BV locality and focusing. -> Area multiplier supported on the original boundary.
- **R7** [claim](#stmt-prop-static-positive) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-static-positive): Static-base construction and complete circle extension. -> Positive interior stationary norm and attached static base.
- **R8** [claim](#stmt-prop-static-euclidean-double) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-static-euclidean-double): Conformal doubling, mass variation and harmonic-coordinate regularity. -> Euclidean filled double.
- **R9** [claim](#stmt-q-converse-prop-adm) / [proof](#proof-stmt-q-converse-prop-adm): Asymptotic plane comparison and vanishing height and coordinate fluxes. -> Invariant ADM mass of the original slice.
- **R10** [claim](#stmt-q3-rigidity-finite-strictness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-q3-rigidity-finite-strictness): Combine the numerical inequality with finite-component equality rigidity. -> Qualitative strictness for disconnected boundary.
- **R11** [claim](#stmt-q4-var-area-localization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-q4-var-area-localization): Compact normal tests, contact regularity and outermostness. -> Area weight concentrated on the horizon.
- **R12** [claim](#stmt-q4-cla-static-classification) / [proof](#proof-stmt-q4-cla-static-classification): Conformal doubling, zero-mass rigidity and Euclidean separation. -> Global Tangherlini static base.
- **R13** [claim](#stmt-q4-rec-embedding) / [proof](#proof-stmt-q4-rec-embedding): Global time primitive and regular horizon coordinates. -> Smooth original-data hypersurface embedding.

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **I-full-cut**: Enclosing area counts the entire intrinsic boundary, including all components and contact with the original boundary.
- **I-original-data**: At equality in the rigidity class, the whole original exterior embeds smoothly into the regular Schwarzschild–Tangherlini exterior, preserving both the metric and second fundamental form.
- **I-sharp-examples**: Admissible static and non-time-symmetric examples realize equality; time symmetry is not a necessary rigidity hypothesis.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **A-auxiliary**: Infer the original metric and second fundamental form from equality of an auxiliary comparison metric. -> Equality of a comparison metric does not establish the required embedding of the original initial data.
- **A-local-area**: Replace the full enclosing infimum with the area of a selected boundary component or a selected candidate cut. -> The selected area can omit boundary components or fail the comparison against every full cut.
- **A-discrete**: Treat a finite sampled metric or a small computed mass-area residual as a certificate of smooth exterior rigidity. -> Samples alone do not establish completeness, asymptotic limits, smoothness, outermostness, or exact equality.
- **A-behind-boundary**: Extend the exterior embedding conclusion to a region behind the horizon boundary. -> The theorem gives no classification of that region.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The results concern smooth initial data on complete exterior manifolds, asymptotic ADM limits, and area comparison over every full enclosing cut. Even the explicit sharp examples require smooth radial graph functions and global enclosure conditions. The source supplies no finite input representation or finite decision procedure for these hypotheses; checking the mass-area formula alone would not certify the original-data embedding.

## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **L-exterior** (formal_scope): The rigidity conclusion identifies the original exterior and its horizon boundary; it does not identify a region behind the boundary. Blocked use: ['Inferring interior black-hole geometry from exterior equality.']
- **L-smooth** (hypothesis): The strong-decay setting requires smooth manifold data, smooth boundary and smooth metric and second fundamental form up to the boundary. Blocked use: ['Applying the smooth rigidity theorem directly to a mesh or a rough metric without establishing its hypotheses.']
- **L-complete-end** (hypothesis): Completeness includes the boundary, and the strong-decay exterior has a single coordinate end outside a compact subset. Blocked use: ['Replacing the exterior by an incomplete truncated domain.', 'Allowing additional uncontrolled ends in the strong-decay equality class.']
- **L-dec** (hypothesis): The dominant energy condition and integrability of the constraint densities are premises. Blocked use: ['Transferring the rigidity conclusion to data violating the dominant energy condition or lacking the required integrability.']
- **L-timelike** (hypothesis): The strong-decay statement imposes a future-timelike ADM vector. Blocked use: ['Using that statement for null or spacelike ADM charge vectors.']
- **L-full-area** (hypothesis): The enclosing infimum counts the entire boundary of each admissible cut, including contact portions. Blocked use: ['Substituting the area of a selected component for the full enclosing area.']
- **L-outermost** (hypothesis): The strong-decay rigidity class requires connected marginal boundary, outer area minimization and exclusion of wholly interior weakly trapped enclosing hypersurfaces. Blocked use: ['Inferring rigidity solely from mass and boundary area while omitting outermostness or outer area minimization.']
- **L-near-equality** (approximation): The embedding conclusion is conditioned on exact equality. A quantitative near-equality stability estimate is ABSENT. Blocked use: ['Treating a small computed deficit as a certificate of proximity to a Schwarzschild–Tangherlini slice.']
- **L-no-gap** (edge_case): Disconnected-boundary strictness is qualitative in the stated finite-component class; no uniform positive deficit is asserted. Blocked use: ['Assigning a universal positive mass–area gap to disconnected horizons.']
- **L-comparison-classes** (hypothesis): Partial-coincidence outermostness permits comparison cuts retaining some entire original components; the connected-boundary statement uses a weaker comparison class. Blocked use: ['Replacing partial-coincidence outermostness by wholly-interior outermostness in the finite-component statement.']
- **L-ambient** (hypothesis): The weak-decay finite-component rigidity statement assumes complete boundaryless ambient data with finitely many asymptotically flat ends. Its chosen exterior has exactly the designated end. Blocked use: ['Dropping the ambient hypotheses when invoking the weak-decay finite-component theorem.']
- **L-auxiliary** (formal_scope): Equality in the numerical bound alone does not identify the original data with an auxiliary comparison metric. Blocked use: ['Claiming original-data rigidity from an auxiliary limiting metric without the original-data variation and reconstruction.']
- **L-envelope** (nonconstructive): The enclosing area derivative is obtained from the minimizing family; following an arbitrary minimizing surface does not establish the derivative of the infimum. Blocked use: ['Differentiating the area of a chosen enclosure as though it were automatically the enclosing area derivative.']
- **L-finite-certificate** (nonconstructive): The multiplier construction uses measures on a family of minimizing enclosures. A finite algorithm certifying the full geometric hypotheses is ABSENT. Blocked use: ['Presenting finite arithmetic checks of model formulas as verification of the full exterior rigidity theorem.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


Equality in the spacetime Penrose inequality identifies the original initial data as a spacelike slice of a Schwarzschild–Tangherlini exterior, smoothly attached to its horizon, under the stated outermostness and decay hypotheses. We prove this in every spatial dimension <i>n</i> ≥ 3 for a strong-decay exterior class and for weaker decay in dimensions three and four. In dimension three the finite-component theorem forces a single spherical horizon and gives qualitative strictness for disconnected boundaries.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
### Introduction

The spacetime Penrose inequality compares the invariant ADM mass of initial data with the least area needed to enclose a trapped boundary. Its model equality cases are spacelike slices of the Schwarzschild–Tangherlini spacetime (Tangherlini 1963) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[Tangherlini1963](#ref-Tangherlini1963)]. Such a slice need not be time-symmetric. Admissible asymptotically boosted slices can have different second fundamental forms and ADM energy–momentum vectors while retaining the same invariant mass. The rigidity question is therefore whether equality determines the original metric and second fundamental form as the induced data of a Schwarzschild–Tangherlini slice.

We prove this conclusion in every spatial dimension $n\ge3$ under strong differentiated decay, and under weaker decay in dimensions three and four. The embedding includes the original horizon in regular spacetime coordinates. In dimension three the finite-component theorem also proves that equality forces the horizon to be connected. The hypotheses and converse statements differ between the three classes; we describe those distinctions before explaining the proof.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### The equality statements and their scope

Write $(E,P)$ for the original ADM energy–momentum vector and $m=(E^2-|P|^2)^{1/2}$ for its invariant mass. Let $a(g)$ be the infimum of the areas of all full enclosing cuts, including every component and every portion coincident with the original boundary $S$. The numerical inequality is $$m\ge F_n(a(g)),\qquad
 F_n(a)=\frac12\left(\frac{a}{\omega_{n-1}}\right)^{(n-2)/(n-1)},
 \qquad \omega_{n-1}=|\mathbb S^{n-1}|.$$ All our equality classes have smooth orientable data satisfying the dominant energy condition, integrable constraint densities and finite ADM limits. Their boundary is marginally outer trapped and outer area-minimizing, so that $a(g)=A:=|S|_g>0$. The chosen closed exterior is complete with its boundary included and has compact complement to one asymptotically flat end. No spin, vacuum, maximality or stationary-development assumption is imposed.

Table <a href="#tab:intro:branches" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="tab:intro:branches">1</a> records the remaining distinctions. Here $O_j(r^{-a})$ includes the coordinate derivative estimates through order $j$; the underlying data are smooth. Wholly-interior outermostness excludes any smooth weakly outer trapped enclosing cut entirely in the open exterior, even if that cut is disconnected. Partial-coincidence outermostness also excludes cuts retaining some entire original boundary components and replacing others by interior components. The precise definitions are given with the theorems.

<div id="tab:intro:branches">

| Class   | Differentiated asymptotics                                                | Horizon, ambient hypothesis and conclusion                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|:--------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| $n\ge3$ | $g-\delta=O_6(r^{-q})$, $K=O_5(r^{-1-q})$, $\frac{n-2}{2}<q<n-2$          | Connected $S$; wholly-interior outermostness; no ambient extension required. Equality and the converse hold in this class (Theorems <a href="#thm:rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:rigidity">5</a> and <a href="#thm:converse" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:converse">6</a>).                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| $n=3$   | $g-\delta=O_2(r^{-q})$, $K=O_1(r^{-1-q})$, $q>\frac12$ on eachambient end | The exterior lies in complete boundaryless data with finitely many AF ends. For finitely many components, partial-coincidence outermostness gives rigidity and connectedness; for connected $S$, wholly-interior outermostness suffices. These are forward statements (Theorems <a href="#q3:intro:rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q3:intro:rigidity">53</a> and <a href="#q3:intro:connected-rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q3:intro:connected-rigidity">54</a>). |
| $n=4$   | $g-\delta=O_2(r^{-q})$, $K=O_1(r^{-1-q})$, $q>1$                          | Connected $S$; wholly-interior outermostness; no ambient extension required. Equality and the converse hold in this weak-decay class (Theorem <a href="#q4:thm:rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q4:thm:rigidity">82</a>).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

</div>

Future timelikeness $E>|P|$ is assumed in the strong and three-dimensional statements. In dimension four it follows from the numerical theorem and positive enclosing area. In the three-dimensional theorem the ambient completeness assumption ensures completeness of the closed chosen exterior; the conclusion concerns only that exterior. No theorem identifies a region behind $S$.

In each branch, equality embeds the entire original exterior, with its given $g$ and $K$, into the regular extension of the exterior of mass $m$. The boundary is a full smooth section of the future horizon or the bifurcation sphere, and the chosen end approaches spatial infinity. The converses include asymptotically boosted slices and compute the invariant mass from the original ADM integrals. The strong class contains examples with $K\not\equiv0$. In the three-dimensional finite-component class, Corollary <a href="#q3:rigidity:finite-strictness" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q3:rigidity:finite-strictness">55</a> gives the further consequence $$S\text{ disconnected}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \sqrt{E^2-|P|^2}>\sqrt{A/(16\pi)}.$$ This is qualitative strictness, with no asserted uniform positive lower bound for the deficit.

Two numerical inputs have distinct roles. The spacetime theorem of *The spacetime Penrose inequality and enclosing area* (OpenAI 2026b, Theorems 1.3, 7.2 and 8.2) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[CompanionNumerical](#ref-CompanionNumerical)] applies to the nearby weakly trapped data used in the variations; they need not satisfy the original pair’s outermostness or area-minimizing hypotheses. The Riemannian theorem of *Conformal flow and the Riemannian Penrose inequality with minimizing frontiers* (OpenAI 2026a, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[CompanionRiemannian](#ref-CompanionRiemannian)] enters later in the all-dimensional classification. We use its numerical bound to prove nonnegative mass and then rigidity for a rough conformal double. Neither input supplies the original-data equality argument.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
#### Why equality must be varied on the original data

The numerical spacetime proof constructs auxiliary metrics and passes to inequalities in a prescribed order. Equality in its final bound does not identify the original pair $(g,K)$ with any one auxiliary metric. We instead use the inequality on admissible variations of $(g,K)$ itself: equality makes the mass–area deficit $m(g,K)-F_n(a(g))$ a constrained minimum.

There are two obstacles to extracting stationary equations from this minimum. A least-area enclosing surface can change when the metric changes. Even when $S$ minimizes area, its own first variation need not be the derivative of the infimum. Moreover, separation of the first variations produces measures on all minimizing enclosures. Interior sheets can therefore contribute an area source to the adjoint equations. This source must be removed before the equations of a stationary spacetime become available.

The geometric step attaches an inner side to $S$ and minimizes full perimeter among sets containing it. Mean-convex spheres confine minimizers for asymptotically flat metric paths. The broader paths needed in dimension three use uniform metric comparison and density bounds instead. Perimeter convergence and continuity for vector measures control the tangent-plane integrals and give the right metric derivative $$a'(g;h)=\min_C\frac12\int_{\partial^*C}
                    \operatorname{tr}_{T\partial^*C}h\,dA_g,$$ where $C$ ranges over all original minimizing enclosures. Thus no differentiable choice of a minimizing surface is needed.

Positive separation then produces a lapse $u$, a shift $X$ and a positive area measure. Causality takes the form $u\ge|X|$, while the Hessian equation initially has a measure source normal to the minimizing sheets. Compact normal tests show that a typical free sheet has both zero mean curvature and zero tangential trace of $K$. In dimensions at most seven it is already smooth, so outermostness removes it. In higher dimensions, atomic sheets are totally geodesic; neighboring nonatomic sheets produce a common positive Jacobi field. Its behavior near singular points, together with a BV zero-set argument, gives a curvature bound that removes the remaining singularities. Smooth outermostness can then be applied.

After localization the interior adjoint is homogeneous. Its stationary development still admits a null-dust alternative. The common stationary argument, Proposition <a href="#prop:static:common-base" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:static:common-base">34</a>, removes the twist and constructs the static base without presupposing a regular interior null set. It retains possible complete ends arising there. The three classifications subsequently resolve these ends in different ways, as shown in Figure <a href="#fig:intro:proof" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:intro:proof">1</a>. In particular, the weak-decay branches derive the harmonic-coordinate estimates needed for compactification; they do not assume strong differentiated decay for the original data.

</figure>

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
#### Mathematical context and attribution

Penrose’s mass–area question arose from black-hole collapse and cosmic censorship (Penrose 1973) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[Penrose1973](#ref-Penrose1973)]. The area in an initial-data formulation requires care. Ben-Dov constructed spherically symmetric data satisfying the dominant energy condition for which the bound using the apparent horizon’s own area fails; he distinguished that area from the minimum area needed to enclose it (Ben-Dov 2004, sec. 1) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[BenDov2004](#ref-BenDov2004)]. This distinction explains the use of $a(g)$ in the numerical inequality and the separate outer area-minimizing assumption in our equality classes.

For time-symmetric data, Huisken and Ilmanen’s weak inverse mean curvature flow proves the three-dimensional bound associated with a connected horizon, while Bray’s conformal flow gives the sharp bound for the total area of a possibly disconnected horizon (Huisken and Ilmanen 2001; Bray 2001) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[HuiskenIlmanen2001](#ref-HuiskenIlmanen2001), [Bray2001](#ref-Bray2001)]. Bray and Lee develop the conformal flow in dimensions below eight (Bray and Lee 2009) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[BrayLee2009](#ref-BrayLee2009)]. Minimizing hulls and smooth-obstacle regularity are central to the inverse mean curvature approach. Here perimeter compactness is combined with Reshetnyak’s continuity principle to differentiate the enclosing infimum as the metric varies (Reshetnyak 1968; Spector 2011) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[Reshetnyak1968](#ref-Reshetnyak1968), [Spector2011](#ref-Spector2011)].

Beyond time symmetry, Bray and Khuri’s generalized Jang construction is an important equality precedent. In their spherically symmetric setting they recover the original metric and second fundamental form as a Schwarzschild spacelike embedding (Bray and Khuri 2010, sec. 4) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[BrayKhuri2010](#ref-BrayKhuri2010)]. Their proposed nonspherical coupled system is conditional on its existence and regularity (Bray and Khuri 2010, sec. 5) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[BrayKhuri2010](#ref-BrayKhuri2010)]. The original-slice conclusion, rather than vanishing of $K$, is thus already integral to the earlier spacetime formulation. The argument here obtains that conclusion by varying the original mass–area deficit after the numerical theorem has been established.

Bartnik’s variational program relates constrained gravitational energy to stationary geometry. In his boundaryless asymptotically flat three-dimensional phase space, critical points of the ADM energy on a fixed constraint level set are characterized by the adjoint constraint equations; future-timelike ADM vectors give the corresponding invariant-mass formulation (R. Bartnik 2005, Theorem 6.1 and Corollary 6.2) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[Bartnik2005PhaseSpace](#ref-Bartnik2005PhaseSpace)]. The Killing-initial-data framework and asymptotic Killing-field estimates of Beig and Chruściel explain how lapse–shift equations encode a spacetime symmetry (Beig and Chruściel 1996, 1997) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[BeigChrusciel1996](#ref-BeigChrusciel1996), [BeigChrusciel1997KID](#ref-BeigChrusciel1997KID)]. For the dominant energy condition, Corvino and Huang introduce a modified constraint operator that accounts for the metric dependence of the momentum norm (Corvino and Huang 2020, sec. 2.2) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[CorvinoHuang2020](#ref-CorvinoHuang2020)]. Huang and Lee relate its adjoint, together with a null-vector identity, to Killing developments with null-fluid stress (Huang and Lee 2024, sec. 6.1) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[HuangLee2024Bartnik](#ref-HuangLee2024Bartnik)].

Hirsch and Huang obtain a strongly stationary vacuum development of the interior for local ADM-mass minimizers with compact boundary, fixed Bartnik data, the dominant energy condition and $E>|P|$, under their stated decay and regularity hypotheses (Hirsch and Huang 2025, Theorem 7) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[HirschHuang2025](#ref-HirschHuang2025)]. Fixing those boundary data fixes $|S|$, but need not fix the least area of all enclosing cuts. Our constrained minimum is therefore a different variational problem: it retains $a(g)$ and the interior source generated by its minimizing enclosures. Their strong maximum principle rules out an interior null point for a causal Killing field $Y$ that is timelike near infinity and satisfies $\operatorname{Ric}(Y,Y)\le0$ (Hirsch and Huang 2025, Theorem 4) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[HirschHuang2025](#ref-HirschHuang2025)]. Here localization first produces the homogeneous adjoint; the stationary construction retains its possible null stress, and the twist argument treats the null set directly.

Static classification has its own ancestry. In three spatial dimensions, Bunting and Masood-ul-Alam used positive mass to remove the connected-horizon assumption in the asymptotically Euclidean static vacuum problem (Bunting and Masood-ul-Alam 1987) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[BuntingMasoodUlAlam1987](#ref-BuntingMasoodUlAlam1987)]. Gibbons, Ida and Shiromizu developed the conformal construction in higher dimensions (Gibbons, Ida, and Shiromizu 2002, sec. 2) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[GibbonsIdaShiromizu2002](#ref-GibbonsIdaShiromizu2002)]. Hwang’s related rigidity theorem concerns complete spin Ricci-flat manifolds with prescribed asymptotically flat behavior and an appropriate circle action with fixed points (Hwang 1998) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[Hwang1998](#ref-Hwang1998)]; this is also a precedent for the circle-extension setting used here. For the present data, we establish the completeness of each double and the required horizon and compactified-point regularity.

The mass inputs are accordingly different in the three branches. Bartnik and Chruściel prove positive energy and parallel-spinor rigidity with a noncompact interior (R. A. Bartnik and Chruściel 2005, Theorem 11.2) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[BartnikChrusciel2005](#ref-BartnikChrusciel2005)]; Cecchini and Zeidler give a smooth Riemannian spin formulation with arbitrary other ends and Euclidean rigidity (Cecchini and Zeidler 2024, Theorem B) <a id="pm-cite-21"></a>[[CecchiniZeidler2024](#ref-CecchiniZeidler2024)]. We supply the spinor argument at the rough regularity of the three-dimensional double. In dimension four, Lesourd, Unger and Yau supply smooth nonspin nonnegative mass for a distinguished asymptotically Schwarzschild end, allowing arbitrary other ends (Lesourd, Unger, and Yau 2024, Theorem 1.2 and Definition 1.9, arXiv version 1) <a id="pm-cite-22"></a>[[LesourdUngerYau2021](#ref-LesourdUngerYau2021)]. We prove the required rigidity by deformation and volume comparison. In the strong-decay branch, the Riemannian numerical companion supplies the mass bound in every dimension from which the rough-double rigidity is derived. None of these applications identifies a merely numerical inequality with an equality theorem.

<a id="pm-h-6"></a>
#### Reading the proof

Section <a href="#sec:setting" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:setting">2</a> states the strong-decay equality theorem and converse. Section <a href="#q:geometry:section" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="q:geometry:section">3</a> establishes the common enclosure geometry and metric derivative. Section <a href="#sec:variation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:variation">4</a> carries out the all-dimensional separation and support localization; its smooth-dimensional shortcut is identified after the contact argument.
